name: AnyPS5
description: Tool for automatic PS5 executables porting to Linux and Windows
one_liner: A technical tool that converts PlayStation 5 game programs so they can run on an ordinary Windows or Linux computer instead of the console.
buyer: Honestly, there is no real paying buyer here: this is a hobbyist reverse-engineering and preservation project for enthusiasts and researchers, not a commercial product.
business_use_cases: A game preservation archivist uses it to keep PS5-era titles playable on ordinary PCs after the original hardware becomes obsolete, for historical and research purposes.
A compatibility researcher studies the project's system-library implementations as part of academic or interoperability research.
A hobbyist streamer showcases running PS5 titles on PC for a tech-curiosity audience, monetized only through ad-supported content, not the tool itself.

money_ideas.idea: There is no clean revenue model here: distributing or charging for a way to run copyrighted console games without licensing is legally fraught.

steal_this: There isn't a legitimate weekend business here; the only real audience is curious developers and preservationists, not paying customers.
